newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Atlas Copco says Prime may need capital.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Copco says Prime may need capital.

text.p: Swedish engineering group Atlas Copco AB said on Thursday it would consider a capital injection for its newly acquired unit, Prime Services Inc., if one was necessary for growth.
Atlas Copco announced the acquisition of U.S. construction equipment leasing company Prime Services for $900 million and $260 million in assumed debt earlier this year.
"Regardless of where growth comes from, whether it is organic or through acquisitions, it requires capital," Atlas Copco finance director Hans Ola Meyer told Reuters.

"Periodically they may need more capital than at other times and then we will provide it. This is nothing negative, though. They are in a growth industry and that's where we want to be. In that case a lot of capital is needed," Meyer said.
"People should not forget that Prime's cash flow is good on its own," he said.

Credit ratings agency Moody's said on Thursday it had downgraded Atlas Copco's short term rating to Prime-2 from Prime-1 since the group's purchase of Prime Services Inc., because of an expected deterioration in its balance sheet.
Moody's also said that in its opinion, Prime Services "might need some further funding as it builds its position in the fast growing and consolidating equipment rentals business sector in the U.S.."

"It's almost as if they believe our future acquisitions will all be entirely debt-financed," said Meyer. "It's too bad this affected their decision. Of course we had hoped they would come to the same conclusion as Standard & Poor's, which maintained its rating.
"We discussed it for a month and it doesn't come as a shock since we knew they were deliberating between downgrading or affirming. We did not agree with their decision," he said.
